## Load packages
```{r setup}
packages <- c("here", "dplyr", "glue", "janitor", "ggplot2", "DT", "stringr", "tidyr")

for (p in packages) {
  if (p %in% rownames(installed.packages())) {
    library(p, character.only = TRUE)
  } else {
    install.packages(p)
    library(p, character.only = TRUE)
  }
}

if (!"rCAX" %in% rownames(installed.packages())) {
  if (!"remotes" %in% rownames(installed.packages())) install.packages("remotes")
  remotes::install_github("nwfsc-cb/rCAX")
}
library(rCAX)

windowsFonts(`Times New Roman` = windowsFont("TT Times New Roman"))
```

## Define data loading and cleaning function
```{r Creating function}
#Pulls a StreamNet HLI table via rCAX, filtered to a single ESU/DPS.
#Defaults are JuvOut (juvenile outmigrants) for Upper Columbia spring
#Chinook. Saves the cleaned data to CSV under pop_label
hli_pull_clean <- function(hli_type = "JuvOut", 
                           esudps_sel = "Salmon, Chinook (Upper Columbia River spring-run ESU)",
                           pop_label = "upper_columbia"){
  hli_raw <- rcax_hli(
    hli_type,
    flist = list(esudps = esudps_sel)
  )
 
  #Age proportion columns weren't previously cast to numeric, unlike
  #totalnatural - if any came back as character (ex. blank-string
  #placeholders instead of true NA), pivot_longer() later combines
  #them into one character column instead of numeric
  hli_clean <- hli_raw %>%
    clean_names() %>%
    mutate(
      totalnatural = as.numeric(totalnatural),
      age0prop = as.numeric(age0prop),
      age1prop = as.numeric(age1prop),
      age2prop = as.numeric(age2prop),
      age3prop = as.numeric(age3prop),
      age4plusprop = as.numeric(age4plusprop)
    )

  write.csv(
    hli_clean,
    here("Results","CSV Files", glue("streamnet_{hli_type}_{pop_label}.csv")),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
 
 hli_clean
}
```

## Call function for each subset of interest
```{r pull juvout data}
juvout_clean <- hli_pull_clean()

juvout_snake_chinook <- hli_pull_clean(
  esudps_sel = "Salmon, Chinook (Snake River spring/summer-run ESU)",
  pop_label = "snake_spring_summer"
)

juvout_snake_steelhead <- hli_pull_clean(
  esudps_sel = "Steelhead (Snake River Basin DPS)",
  pop_label = "snake_steelhead"
)

juvout_upper_col_steelhead <- hli_pull_clean(
  esudps_sel = "Steelhead (Upper Columbia River DPS)",
  pop_label = "upper_columbia_steelhead"
)

nrow(juvout_clean)
nrow(juvout_snake_chinook)
nrow(juvout_snake_steelhead)
nrow(juvout_upper_col_steelhead)
```

## Explore additional data issues, data summaries, and visualization
```{r define presentation theme and export function}
presentation_theme <- theme(
  text = element_text(family = "Times New Roman", face = "bold", size = 22),
  plot.title = element_text(size = 28, face = "bold"),
  axis.title = element_text(size = 22),
  axis.text = element_text(size = 18),
  strip.text = element_text(size = 18),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 18),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 20)
)

ggsave_presentation <- function(filename, height = 7.5, width = 13.33, dpi = 300){
  ggsave(here("Results", "Figures", filename), height = height, width = width, dpi = dpi)
}

#Splits populationname into location_name and run_species. Most names
#use " - " as a separator; some have no dash and instead end in a
#run/species phrase, which is matched and stripped separately
split_pop_name <- function(df){
  split_cols <- stringr::str_split_fixed(df$populationname, " - ", n = 2)
  
  location_name <- split_cols[, 1]
  run_species <- split_cols[, 2]
  
  run_species_patterns <- c(
    "spring Chinook Salmon", "summer Chinook Salmon", "fall Chinook Salmon",
    "spring/summer Chinook Salmon", "summer Steelhead", "spring Steelhead"
  )
  
  no_dash <- run_species == ""
  
  for (pattern in run_species_patterns) {
    matches <- no_dash & endsWith(location_name, paste0(" ", pattern))
    run_species[matches] <- pattern
    location_name[matches] <- trimws(sub(paste0(" ", pattern, "$"), "", location_name[matches]))
  }
  
  df %>%
    mutate(
      location_name = location_name,
      run_species = run_species
    )
}
```

```{r define exploration functions}
#Missingness by column, plus a population count
na_summary_function <- function(data){
  data %>% count(populationname) %>% print()
  
  na_summary <- data.frame(
    column_name = colnames(data),
    n_missing = colSums(is.na(data))
  )
  datatable(na_summary)
}

plot_juvout_function <- function(data, plot_title, file_name){
  data %>%
    split_pop_name() %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = outmigrationyear, y = totalnatural, color = location_name)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    facet_wrap(~ location_name) +
    labs(title = plot_title, x = "Year", y = "Total Natural Outmigrants") +
    theme(legend.position = "none") +
    presentation_theme +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 13))
  ggsave_presentation(file_name)
}

#Data coverage timeline: blue = totalnatural present, dark red = row
#exists but totalnatural is NA, light red = no row at all
coverage_juvout_function <- function(data, plot_title, file_name){
  pop_data <- data %>%
    filter(!is.na(outmigrationyear)) %>%
    split_pop_name() %>%
    select(location_name, outmigrationyear, totalnatural)
  
  year_range <- seq(min(pop_data$outmigrationyear), max(pop_data$outmigrationyear))
  populations <- unique(pop_data$location_name)
  
  full_grid <- data.frame()
  for (pop in populations) {
    full_grid <- bind_rows(full_grid, data.frame(location_name = pop, outmigrationyear = year_range))
  }
  
  pop_data_summary <- pop_data %>%
    group_by(location_name, outmigrationyear) %>%
    summarize(has_row = TRUE, has_value = any(!is.na(totalnatural)), .groups = "drop")
  
  data_status <- full_grid %>%
    left_join(pop_data_summary, by = c("location_name", "outmigrationyear")) %>%
    mutate(
      status = case_when(
        is.na(has_row) ~ "No data reported",
        has_value ~ "Data available",
        TRUE ~ "NA"
      )
    )
  
  data_status %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = outmigrationyear, y = location_name, fill = status)) +
    geom_tile(height = 0.9, width = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(
      "Data available" = "blue",
      "NA" = "darkred",
      "No data reported" = "lightcoral"
    )) +
    labs(title = plot_title, x = "Year", y = NULL, fill = "Status") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
    presentation_theme +
    theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 22))
  
  ggsave_presentation(file_name)
}

#Age-class coverage per population. file_prefix should not include an
#extension - each population's file is saved separately
coverage_juvout_age_function <- function(data, plot_title, file_prefix){
  populations <- unique(data$populationname)
  
  for (pop in populations) {
    pop_data <- data %>% filter(populationname == pop)
    
    data_long <- bind_rows(
      pop_data %>% mutate(age_label = "Age 0", age_value = age0prop),
      pop_data %>% mutate(age_label = "Age 1", age_value = age1prop),
      pop_data %>% mutate(age_label = "Age 2", age_value = age2prop),
      pop_data %>% mutate(age_label = "Age 3", age_value = age3prop),
      pop_data %>% mutate(age_label = "Age 4+", age_value = age4plusprop)
    ) %>%
      select(age_label, outmigrationyear, age_value) %>%
      filter(!is.na(outmigrationyear))
    
    year_range <- seq(min(data_long$outmigrationyear), max(data_long$outmigrationyear))
    age_labels <- unique(data_long$age_label)
    
    full_grid <- data.frame()
    for (a in age_labels) {
      full_grid <- bind_rows(full_grid, data.frame(age_label = a, outmigrationyear = year_range))
    }
    
    data_status <- full_grid %>%
      left_join(
        data_long %>%
          group_by(age_label, outmigrationyear) %>%
          summarize(has_row = TRUE, has_value = any(!is.na(age_value)), .groups = "drop"),
        by = c("age_label", "outmigrationyear")
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        status = case_when(
          is.na(has_row) ~ "No data reported",
          has_value ~ "Data available",
          TRUE ~ "NA"
        )
      )
    
    pop_location <- data.frame(populationname = pop) %>% split_pop_name() %>% pull(location_name)
    pop_title <- glue("{plot_title}\n{pop_location}")
    pop_file_name <- glue("{file_prefix}_{pop}.png")
    
    print(
      data_status %>%
        ggplot(aes(x = outmigrationyear, y = age_label, fill = status)) +
        geom_tile(height = 0.9, width = 1) +
        scale_fill_manual(values = c(
          "Data available" = "blue",
          "NA" = "darkred",
          "No data reported" = "lightcoral"
        )) +
        labs(title = pop_title, x = "Year", y = NULL, fill = "Status") +
        theme_bw() +
        theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()) +
        presentation_theme
    )
    
    ggsave_presentation(pop_file_name)
  }
}

#Single-panel line plot, colored by population, for one basin/species
#subset
plot_juvout_single_panel_function <- function(data, plot_title, file_name){
  data %>%
    split_pop_name() %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = outmigrationyear, y = totalnatural, color = location_name)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(title = plot_title, x = "Year", y = "Total Natural Outmigrants", color = "Population") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    presentation_theme
  ggsave_presentation(file_name)
}

#Same single-panel line plot as plot_juvout_single_panel_function, but
#on a log10 y-axis. Proportional changes (ex. a population dropping
#90%) are visually comparable across populations of very different
#scale, which gets flattened out on a linear axis
plot_juvout_log_scale_function <- function(data, plot_title, file_name){
  data %>%
    split_pop_name() %>%
    filter(!is.na(totalnatural), totalnatural > 0) %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = outmigrationyear, y = totalnatural, color = location_name)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    scale_y_log10(labels = scales::comma) +
    labs(title = plot_title, x = "Year", y = "Total Natural Outmigrants (log scale)", color = "Population") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    presentation_theme
  ggsave_presentation(file_name)
}

#Stacked area of age-class proportions per year, one panel per
#population. Shows whether a population's age structure has shifted
#over time (ex. trending toward more subyearling outmigrants).
#geom_area(position = "fill") rescales whatever age classes ARE
#reported to sum to 100% each year - a population/year with fewer
#than 5 non-NA age classes will show its available classes filling
#the full bar rather than a visible gap
plot_age_composition_function <- function(data, plot_title, file_name){
  data_long <- data %>%
    split_pop_name() %>%
    filter(!is.na(outmigrationyear)) %>%
    select(location_name, outmigrationyear, age0prop, age1prop, age2prop, age3prop, age4plusprop) %>%
    tidyr::pivot_longer(
      cols = c(age0prop, age1prop, age2prop, age3prop, age4plusprop),
      names_to = "age_class", values_to = "proportion"
    ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(proportion)) %>%
    mutate(
      age_class = case_when(
        age_class == "age0prop" ~ "Age 0",
        age_class == "age1prop" ~ "Age 1",
        age_class == "age2prop" ~ "Age 2",
        age_class == "age3prop" ~ "Age 3",
        age_class == "age4plusprop" ~ "Age 4+"
      ),
      age_class = factor(age_class, levels = c("Age 0", "Age 1", "Age 2", "Age 3", "Age 4+"))
    )
  
  data_long %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = outmigrationyear, y = proportion, fill = age_class)) +
    geom_area(position = "fill") +
    facet_wrap(~ location_name) +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(title = plot_title, x = "Year", y = "Proportion of Outmigrants", fill = "Age Class") +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom") +
    presentation_theme +
    theme(strip.text = element_text(size = 13))
  
  ggsave_presentation(file_name)
}

#Horizontal bar of first-to-last outmigration year per population,
#across all four subsets combined. Bar length is the SPAN between
#first and last reported year, not a count of years with data - a
#population could have a wide span but many missing years within it.
#Fill color (n_years, the actual count of years with data) shows that
#separately, so a long-but-sparse span reads differently from a
#long-and-consistent one
plot_juvout_year_span_function <- function(){
  span_data <- bind_rows(
    juvout_clean %>% split_pop_name() %>% mutate(subset_label = "UC Chinook"),
    juvout_snake_chinook %>% split_pop_name() %>% mutate(subset_label = "Snake Chinook"),
    juvout_upper_col_steelhead %>% split_pop_name() %>% mutate(subset_label = "UC Steelhead"),
    juvout_snake_steelhead %>% split_pop_name() %>% mutate(subset_label = "Snake Steelhead")
  ) %>%
    filter(!is.na(outmigrationyear), !is.na(totalnatural)) %>%
    mutate(pop_label = paste(location_name, "-", subset_label)) %>%
    group_by(pop_label) %>%
    summarize(first_year = min(outmigrationyear), last_year = max(outmigrationyear), n_years = n())
  
  span_data %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = reorder(pop_label, last_year - first_year), y = last_year - first_year, fill = n_years)) +
    geom_col() +
    coord_flip() +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightcoral", high = "blue") +
    labs(title = "JuvOut Time Series Span by Population",
         x = NULL, y = "Years Between First and Last Reported Value", fill = "# Years\nw/ Data") +
    presentation_theme +
    theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))
  
  ggsave_presentation("juvout_year_span_all_subsets.png", height = 7,5, width = 13.33)
}
```
